title: Year 3: year close
hook: the summit sit: look back over the year, from the snake sacrifice to the candle flame

segments.voice: Yesterday: Shvetaketu, home and proud, who became a beginner again with teach me, sir.

Day six hundred ninety-seven. A king's great snake sacrifice, and a storyteller who begins the story of the Bharatas. That's where this year started. Since then: a vow that cost Bhishma everything, a house built to burn, a game of dice, and Draupadi's question the hall could not answer. Years in the forest. A lake, and a voice asking questions before anyone could drink. A chariot between two armies, and a song. Then a baby carried across a flooded river, a hill lifted over a village in the rain, a flute. Today, the summit sit: year three, looked at whole.
screen: `DAY 697: THE SNAKE SACRIFICE.` → `A WAR, A SONG, A CHILD, A FLUTE.` → `THE YEAR, LOOKED AT WHOLE.`

segments.voice: The Mahabharata came as a serial: the cousins, the exile, the war, Bhishma on his bed of arrows, the last journey with a dog that would not be left behind. Then the Bhagavata's Krishna as a child in Vraja: the butter thief, the mouth with the whole universe inside it, Govardhan held up over the village. Then the saints of bhakti: Andal, Tukaram, Kabir, Mirabai, singing in their own languages. Then the modern teachers: Ramakrishna, Vivekananda, Ramana asking who am I, Tagore's song offerings. Then the lineage tracks, and the practices: breath, japa, yoga nidra, the gaze on a flame. Now go back to the lake. In the Vana Parva, a voice from the water warns each brother who tries to drink. They drink anyway, and fall. Only Yudhishthira stops to answer its questions. One of them: what is the most wonderful thing? His answer, in paraphrase: every day, living beings go to the house of Death, and the ones who remain want to stay forever. What could be more wonderful than that? His wonder is at how easily the living forget what they see every day. Another year has gone. Faces in the stories have come and gone, and some listeners will have lost someone real since day six hundred ninety-seven. A year of sits is a small way of not forgetting: noticing, day by day, that you are among the ones who remain, for now, and that the time is worth using.
screen: `THE GREAT STORY: A WAR AND A SONG.` · `A CHILD IN VRAJA, THEN THE SAINTS.` · `THE TEACHERS, THEN THE PRACTICES.` · `WHAT IS THE MOST WONDERFUL THING?` · then, large: `AMONG THE ONES WHO REMAIN.`

segments.voice: Let three faces from this year come to mind, maybe someone from the great story, someone who sang, someone who taught, and let each stand there for a breath, unranked, before you let them go. Then notice: the breath is still coming, and you are still here, among the ones who remain. If you pray, give thanks for the year in the words you already use; if you don't, let the breath be the thanks.
Year three. The great story, the child in Vraja, the saints, the teachers, and the practices, held together at the summit before the next ranges.
Your line: Year three, year close. It began with one storyteller, and now the stories are yours too. That's day one thousand sixty.

howItsDone: Yudhishthira's answers to the Yaksha at the lake in the Mahabharata's Vana Parva are retold in Hindu homes and talks, and his answer about what is most wonderful is sometimes recalled at times of loss or looking back.

chat.says: At the lake, what did Yudhishthira call the most wonderful thing?
options: That every day beings go to Death, yet those who remain want to stay forever.
That the sun still rises every morning, no matter what happened the day before.
That a good king can rule a whole kingdom without ever feeling afraid.
chat.meaning: In the Vana Parva, his wonder is how easily the living forget what they see every day: they remain only for now.

Vraja.meaning: the cowherd country where Krishna grew up

notes: Year three close. The look-back follows the year-three outline and the titles of the year-three scripts on disk (697 snake sacrifice frame; Bhishma's vow; the lac house; the dice game; Draupadi's question; the Yaksha, 800–807; the Gita in place; Krishna's childhood; Andal, Tukaram, Kabir, Mirabai; Ramakrishna, Vivekananda, Ramana, Tagore; trataka). Confirm every item was in fact taught, especially Mirabai, Kabir and the last journey with the dog.

Editor pass: the teach read Yudhishthira's 'most wonderful thing' as praise for the listener still being alive ('he doesn't call that foolish, he calls it a wonder'); the answer marvels at how the living forget death, so the close now reads it that way, the large screen line became 'among the ones who remain', the third myth item (which repeated the misreading) was replaced, and the trapdoor adjusted. 'Some readers' became 'some listeners'; howItsDone 'often' softened. Day 697 confirmed on disk as the snake-sacrifice frame.

Audit (2026-10-01): content checked against Vana Parva (four brothers drink despite the warning and fall; Yudhishthira answers; the 'most wonderful' answer paraphrased accurately) and against 1047-1053 (every look-back item was taught). Only change: the trapdoor's second floor was garbled ('the ones who remain remain only for now'); rewritten. The look-back overlaps 1047's summit sit on the great story by design (year close).
The Yaksha's 'most wonderful thing' was already taught around days 805–806; it is reused here as a callback, not a new teaching.

Yaksha answer paraphrased (Vana Parva, Yaksha-prashna: ahany ahani bhūtāni gacchantīha yamālayam / śeṣāḥ sthāvaram icchanti kim āścaryam ataḥ param). Ganguli's PD translation was not quoted (not on the validator list). Confirm the Devanagari and pronunciation of āścarya.
'Govardhan held up over the village' follows the Bhagavata's image (Krishna held the hill up like a child holds a mushroom/umbrella); confirm it matches how the path told it.
Carry 'Year 3: year close' keeps the index's capital, which the validator may warn about; it must match the index exactly.
